data.gender_notes: Sagar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Sagar is an ancient sage and king who is the father of the Asuras. His name means 'ocean' or 'deep' and symbolizes the vastness and abundance of life. The name Sagar carries the meaning “Ocean, Deep, Abundant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Sagar usually hope their child will grow to embody ocean, deep, abundant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the deep and boundless nature of the universe.
data.etymology: Sagar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ocean, Deep, Abundant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sagar total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: Sagar is a popular and revered name among Hindus, originating from ancient mythology. The name carries significant cultural significance as it is associated with a powerful king and sage who played a crucial role in Hindu mythology. According to myth, Sagar was the father of the Asuras, beings who represent non-human races or demigods. The term 'asura' is derived from the word 'asu' meaning 'breath' or 'life', making Sagar a symbol of the sustainer of life.
data.spiritual_significance: At a spiritual level, Sagar represents the vastness and depth of life, unending and vast as the ocean. It signifies the belief in the abundance of life and the inner potential for growth and transformation. The name Sagar also holds the idea of courage and resilience, as demonstrated by the sage character in Hindu mythology who led a grand sacrifice to seek divine blessings. Thus, it serves as a reminder of the inner strength to overcome challenges and achieve spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sagar symbolizes the infinite, universal ocean of consciousness and knowledge. It represents the deep, vast expanse of the cosmos and our inner selves, where wisdom and truth reside.

vedic_reference.note: Derived from the Sanskrit word सागर (sāgara), meaning 'ocean'. In Hindu mythology, Sagar is the name of a great sage and the king of the seas. He is also the father of the sage Kapila and the grandfather of the great sage Bhagiratha.

historical_references.reference: The Hindu epic Mahabharata tells the story of King Asvasena of the Lunar Dynasty. King Asvasena was once cursed by sage Durvasa, which led him to name his son as Sagar. This event occurred during the Mahabharata period, around 3000 BCE.
historical_references.context: King Asvasena was cursed by sage Durvasa and named his son as Sagar.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Sagar is found in the Puranas, specifically in the Vayu Purana. In this reference, Sagar is described as the king of the Ikshvaku dynasty, who performed a grand sacrifice (Ashvamedha Yajna) to secure his kingdom and the blessings of the gods. This event is believed to have occurred around 5000 BCE.
historical_references.context: King Sagar of the Ikshvaku dynasty performed a grand sacrifice to secure his kingdom and the blessings of the gods.

In movies and TV shows, Sagar is a popular name for characters in various productions, such as the character 'Sagar' in the TV series 'Asur'. Lastly, on social media, 'Sagar' is a common name and has over 10,000 users on various platforms like Facebook and Twitter.
